items.title: Arc rail Phase 1: contracts deployed + one real session (Arc Testnet)

items.title: Arc rail Phase 2: PlayerCore + self-hosted gasless relayer (Arc Testnet)
items.summary: PlayerCore deployed (the single per-player account: lives, points, premium, per-game buckets). The self-hosted relayer submitted every write and paid the gas; the player signed nothing and paid nothing. A full game cost 0.011034 USDC, all paid by the app. No paid sponsorship platform is used.
items.decision: Gasless model proven. Player cost is zero by construction.

items.title: Arc rail Phase 3: O(1) batching + TTL expiry (Arc Testnet)
items.summary: One transaction commits a Merkle root for N games, so the gas is flat (O(1)) and the per-game cost falls as 1/N. TTL was proven live: a game opened with a 2 second TTL was expired permissionlessly after the deadline.
items.decision: Batching is the cost lever. The window policy is a config choice.

items.title: Arc rail settlement window: launch economics
items.summary: The relayer flushes when the pending batch reaches N games OR the window reaches T seconds, whichever first, and always flushes at window close even with one game. This table shows what a window costs at very low launch volume (10 games a day).
items.decision: SUPERSEDED by arc-batch-cost-locked (owner-locked 2026-09-19): launch setting is 100 matches or 1h, empty windows skipped. See that entry for the measured table.

sections.heading: Cost per window at 10 games a day
When volume grows (N flushes first)
bullets: Receipts while a batch is open: each game gets an instant app-signed receipt (including the dice-seed hash published before the game), labelled pending; at flush it upgrades to an on-chain receipt with that game's own Merkle proof and the batch transaction hash. No game waits on another.
To have an on-chain link the moment a game ends, a config knob anchors each start on-chain for about 0.00243 USDC (about 1 USD per 400 games at launch volume).

items.title: GFG-BS batch cost, LOCKED setting (100 matches or 1h, skip empty) and what a flush commits
items.summary: The final launch setting and its real cost. A flush happens when 100 matches are pending OR the OLDEST pending match is 1 hour old, and an EMPTY window never flushes (no pending = no transaction = no cost). Cost is PER FLUSH, never per match or per move: games in the same burst of play share ONE transaction. Measured on Arc: a flush is a single O(1) transaction (~136,000 gas at a 2-match flush; the tx sends only the Merkle root, count and block range, so gas does not grow with the number of matches). Launch reality (3-5 games a day in a few bursts) costs about 0.0006 to 0.002 USDC a day, under the 0.01/day target.
items.decision: LOCKED: BATCH_MAX = 100 matches, BATCH_MAX_AGE = 1h, empty windows always skipped. Both are config values, never code.

sections.heading: Daily cost for a starter (what you actually pay)
Cost per 1,000 gameplays (reporting unit, not a threshold)
What a flush commits (verifiability)
paragraphs: On-chain: ONE Merkle root, with ONE leaf per match (gameId + moveDigest + resultHash + moveCount). The batch transaction sends only the root, the count and the block range, so its gas is O(1) no matter how many matches it carries.

ALWAYS verifiable: the match happened, who played (the MatchStarted event), its move count, its result digest, and that the digest carries BOTH players signatures (so a result cannot be forged). Membership in the root is provable with a Merkle proof.

VERIFIABLE ON DEMAND: the actual move list stays off-chain but is bound to the signed digest, so it becomes checkable the moment it is revealed (the dispute/reveal path). Nothing is taken on trust: the chain permanently commits players + move count + result + both signatures.

sections.heading: Timing rule (per match, not per clock hour)
paragraphs: Every match starts its OWN 1-hour timer when it finishes. A flush happens when 100 matches are pending OR the oldest pending match reaches 1 hour, whichever comes first. A match is swept by the NEXT flush after it finishes, so an overlapping match is never charged twice and never waits a full hour if a flush already happened.
PRACTICAL RULE: you pay one flush per BURST of play, not per game and not per hour of the day. Games in the same session share one flush.
